# dlanv2

> Computes the Schur factorization of a real 2-by-2 nonsymmetric matrix in standard form.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlanv2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlanv2';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlanv2( A, B, C, D, rt1r, rt1i, rt2r, rt2i, cs, sn ) → void
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `A` | `Float64Array` | **in/out** · The (1,1) element of the matrix |
| `B` | `Float64Array` | **in/out** · The (1,2) element of the matrix |
| `C` | `Float64Array` | **in/out** · The (2,1) element of the matrix |
| `D` | `Float64Array` | **in/out** · The (2,2) element of the matrix |
| `rt1r` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `rt1r` |
| `rt1i` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `rt1i` |
| `rt2r` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `rt2r` |
| `rt2i` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the real and imaginary parts of the eigenvalues |
| `cs` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `cs` |
| `sn` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): parameters of the rotation matrix |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `D`: On entry, the elements of the input matrix. On exit, they are overwritten by the elements of the standardised Schur form.
- `rt2i`: The real and imaginary parts of the eigenvalues. If the eigenvalues are a complex conjugate pair, $\mathrm{RT1I} > 0$.
- `sn`: Parameters of the rotation matrix.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlanv2.ndarray( A, B, C, D, rt1r, rt1i, rt2r, rt2i, cs, sn ) → void
```

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import dlanv2 from '../base/lib/base.js';

// Compute the Schur factorization of a 2x2 matrix with real eigenvalues:
const a = new Float64Array( 1 );
const b = new Float64Array( 1 );
const c = new Float64Array( 1 );
const d = new Float64Array( 1 );
const rt1r = new Float64Array( 1 );
const rt1i = new Float64Array( 1 );
const rt2r = new Float64Array( 1 );
const rt2i = new Float64Array( 1 );
const cs = new Float64Array( 1 );
const sn = new Float64Array( 1 );

a[ 0 ] = 4.0;
b[ 0 ] = 1.0;
c[ 0 ] = 2.0;
d[ 0 ] = 3.0;
dlanv2( a, b, c, d, rt1r, rt1i, rt2r, rt2i, cs, sn );
console.log( 'Real eigenvalue case:' ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( '  Schur form: A=' + a[ 0 ] + ', B=' + b[ 0 ] + ', C=' + c[ 0 ] + ', D=' + d[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console, max-len
console.log( '  Eigenvalues: (' + rt1r[ 0 ] + ' + ' + rt1i[ 0 ] + 'i), (' + rt2r[ 0 ] + ' + ' + rt2i[ 0 ] + 'i)' ); // eslint-disable-line no-console, max-len
console.log( '  Rotation: cs=' + cs[ 0 ] + ', sn=' + sn[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console, max-len

// Compute the Schur factorization of a 2x2 matrix with complex eigenvalues:
a[ 0 ] = 1.0;
b[ 0 ] = -5.0;
c[ 0 ] = 1.0;
d[ 0 ] = 1.0;
dlanv2( a, b, c, d, rt1r, rt1i, rt2r, rt2i, cs, sn );
console.log( '\nComplex eigenvalue case:' ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( '  Schur form: A=' + a[ 0 ] + ', B=' + b[ 0 ] + ', C=' + c[ 0 ] + ', D=' + d[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console, max-len
console.log( '  Eigenvalues: (' + rt1r[ 0 ] + ' + ' + rt1i[ 0 ] + 'i), (' + rt2r[ 0 ] + ' + ' + rt2i[ 0 ] + 'i)' ); // eslint-disable-line no-console, max-len
console.log( '  Rotation: cs=' + cs[ 0 ] + ', sn=' + sn[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console, max-len
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLANV2`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLANV2 computes the Schur factorization of a real 2-by-2 nonsymmetric matrix in standard form:

$$
\begin{bmatrix} A & B \\ C & D \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{CS} & -\mathrm{SN} \\ \mathrm{SN} & \mathrm{CS} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{AA} & \mathrm{BB} \\ \mathrm{CC} & \mathrm{DD} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{CS} & \mathrm{SN} \\ -\mathrm{SN} & \mathrm{CS} \end{bmatrix}
$$

where either 1) $\mathrm{CC} = 0$ so that AA and DD are real eigenvalues of the matrix, or 2) $\mathrm{AA} = \mathrm{DD}$ and $\mathrm{BB} \, \mathrm{CC} < 0$, so that AA + or - sqrt(BB\*CC) are complex conjugate eigenvalues.

### Further Details

Modified by V. Sima, Research Institute for Informatics, Bucharest, Romania, to reduce the risk of cancellation errors, when computing real eigenvalues, and to ensure, if possible, that $\lvert \mathrm{RT1R} \rvert \ge \lvert \mathrm{RT2R} \rvert$.

</section>
